title: Best GPU Sandboxes for AI Agents (2026)
summary: Compare the best GPU sandboxes for AI agents in 2026. Thunder Compute, Daytona and Modal ranked on GPU types, preemption, isolation and H100 price.
body_markdown:
The best GPU sandboxes for AI agents in 2026 are Thunder Compute, Daytona and Modal. Thunder Compute offers the lowest on-demand H100 rate of the three. Daytona offers flexible hardware and cheaper spot capacity. Modal has the widest GPU range, from T4 to B300, on a broader serverless platform.


Most agent sandboxes are CPU-only, and only a few sandbox platforms put a GPU inside the sandbox itself. This guide compares three managed GPU sandbox platforms, with verified prices and limits.


**Takeaways**


- **Thunder Compute offers the cheapest non-preemptible H100 sandbox** of the three, at $2.95/hr.
- **Daytona offers the most flexibility** , with eight GPU types and spot capacity.
- **Modal has the widest GPU range** , from T4 to B300, but its GPU sandboxes are preemptible only.
- **E2B and Vercel Sandbox are CPU-only** , so they don't qualify as GPU sandboxes.


## How We Picked the Top Sandbox Platforms for AI Agents


A platform qualified only if agent code can use a GPU inside the sandbox. A separate GPU inference API doesn't count, because generated code, its data and the GPU must share one isolation boundary.


The comparison covers the factors that decide agent workloads:


- GPU types
- On-demand versus preemptible capacity
- Isolation model
- Session length and persistence
- The hourly rate for an H100

## 1. Thunder Compute: Non-Preemptible H100s at the Lowest On-Demand Rate


Thunder Compute offers the cheapest non-preemptible H100 sandbox of the three, at $2.95/hr against $3.95/hr at Modal and Daytona on-demand. Every Thunder Compute sandbox is non-preemptible. Long evals and RL runs finish at the quoted price instead of being evicted and rerun.


Each Thunder Compute sandbox is a Firecracker microVM (a lightweight, hardware-isolated VM). Sandboxes are created through a[Python SDK](https://github.com/Thunder-Compute/thunder-sandbox) . Commands run as durable jobs, and outbound network access can be open, blocked or restricted to allowlists.


**Best for:** long evals, RL rollouts and inference loops where interruptions are costly.


> [Request GPU sandbox access on Thunder Compute.](https://www.thundercompute.com/products/sandboxes)


## 2. Daytona: Flexible Hardware and Spot Capacity


Daytona supports eight GPU types, including AMD MI355X and consumer RTX 4090 and 5090 cards. Daytona passes a dedicated physical GPU into each sandbox VM via VFIO (Linux's device passthrough framework), so GPUs are never shared.


Daytona's spot tier is the cheapest H100 sandbox of the three, at $2.27/hr. Spot sandboxes can be terminated without notice, and evicted sandboxes stay retrievable for 24 hours. On-demand H100s cost $3.95/hr, and on-demand requests wait for capacity when GPUs run out.


Daytona GPU sandboxes are ephemeral and are deleted when stopped. They auto-stop after 15 idle minutes by default. Teams that must keep compute in their own infrastructure can attach their own machines through custom regions.


**Best for:** non-H100 hardware and interruptible batch jobs that can use spot pricing.


## 3. Modal: The Widest GPU Range on a Serverless Platform


Modal offers a broad GPU range from T4 to B300 cards. Modal Sandboxes sit inside a larger serverless platform for inference, training and batch jobs. Teams already running workloads on Modal can add sandboxes without another vendor.


Modal isolates sandboxes with gVisor (Google's user-space kernel). Modal GPU sandboxes are preemptible only, at Modal's standard GPU rates. Sessions default to 5 minutes, with a maximum of 24 hours. Sandbox CPU and memory cost more than Modal's regular functions, and region selection adds a 1.15x or 1.75x multiplier.


Modal leads on persistence, with volumes and filesystem snapshots.


**Best for:** teams already on Modal, and workloads that need a GPU the other platforms don't offer, such as T4, L4 or L40S.


## Other Sandbox Providers for Code Execution


[NVIDIA OpenShell](https://docs.nvidia.com/openshell/how-it-works/sandboxes/overview) also supports GPUs in sandboxed environments. It is an open-source sandbox runtime with a GPU request flag, currently in[alpha](https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell) .


Popular code sandboxes such as E2B and[Vercel Sandbox](https://vercel.com/docs/sandbox/concepts) are CPU-only. They work well for agents that run ordinary code and call a hosted model API. They don't fit workloads that need a GPU inside the sandbox.


## Best Sandbox for Production AI Agents: Picks by Workload


### RL Training and Rollouts


RL training needs a non-preemptible sandbox, because a rollout lost to eviction must be rerun and can slow down training. Thunder Compute offers the cheapest non-preemptible H100 of the three.


### Coding-Agent Evals


Coding-agent evals against self-hosted models need a GPU, a fresh environment per task and predictable cost across thousands of runs. Thunder Compute's non-preemptible H100s fit evals. Daytona's spot tier can cut eval costs if your harness retries interrupted tasks.


### Local-Model Inference Inside the Agent Loop


Agents that call a local model need a GPU sized to that model. A single H100 with 80GB of memory fits many small and mid-sized open models. Very large models may need Modal's H200 and B200 options.

## Last Thoughts on the Best GPU Sandboxes


Each of the three managed GPU sandbox platforms leads on a different axis. Thunder Compute wins on non-preemptible H100 pricing, Daytona on hardware flexibility and spot capacity, and Modal on GPU range and platform breadth.


Start by weighing the workload's GPU, its tolerance for interruption and its budget per run.


## FAQ


### What Is the Best Sandbox for AI Agents That Need a GPU?


The best GPU sandbox depends on the workload. Thunder Compute leads for non-preemptible H100 jobs, Daytona for spot capacity, and Modal for the widest GPU range.


### Which Sandbox Platforms Support GPUs Inside the Sandbox?


As of October 2026, Thunder Compute, Daytona and Modal offer managed GPU sandboxes. E2B and Vercel Sandbox are CPU-only.


### What Isolation Does Each GPU Sandbox Platform Use?


Thunder Compute uses Firecracker microVMs, Daytona uses sandbox VMs with VFIO GPU passthrough, and Modal uses gVisor.


### Can I Bring My Own Compute to a GPU Sandbox Platform?


Daytona lets teams attach their own machines through custom regions. Modal is managed only, and Thunder Compute doesn't document a bring-your-own-compute option.


### What Is the Fastest Sandbox for AI Agents?


GPU sandboxes typically start more slowly than CPU sandboxes, because a GPU has to be allocated and initialized. Comparable GPU startup benchmarks are hard to find, so measure startup time with your own image.
